query: For an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating susceptible to progressive plastic deformation during continuous loading, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain its creep resistance? Specify the governing factor and rationale, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, the operating boundaries under sustained stress, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The creep resistance of an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating is primarily governed by the dynamic precipitation of coherent precipitates along grain boundaries, which exert a boundary obstacle stress that prevents the annihilation of moving dislocations at the boundaries, thereby reducing the effective stress controlling dislocation velocity.
generation.structural_mediator: Dynamic precipitation of coherent precipitates along grain boundaries
generation.mechanism: Precipitation hardening, dislocation interactions, and vacancy generation
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased creep resistance, reduced dislocation velocity, and enhanced structural stability
generation.boundary: Temperature range of 500-600 °C, stress levels above 100 MPa
generation.uncertainty: The exact role of grain boundary structure and chemistry on precipitation hardening, and the potential effects of other microstructural features, such as stacking faults and twin boundaries, on creep resistance

falsification_experiment.design: In situ TEM or synchrotron X-ray diffraction experiments to monitor microstructural evolution under stress
measurements: Dislocation velocity, precipitation density, grain boundary structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the creep resistance of the FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating is not significantly improved by dynamic precipitation of coherent precipitates along grain boundaries, as evidenced by a lack of correlation between precipitation density and dislocation velocity, then the hypothesis is falsified (threshold: <10% increase in creep resistance)
